spec_features.spec_quote: Each run has a hard cap on iterations (`max_iters`, default 10) and wall-clock. No unbounded loops.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:117 `for i in range(max_iters):` bounds the loop; agent_loop.py:118-120 `if time.time()-t0 > wall_clock_cap_s: result.error='wall_clock_cap_reached'; break`. Both caps are checked and break execution. Defaults max_iters=10 (runner.py ExperimentConfig, config/experiment.yaml), wall_clock_cap_s=600 passed through run_episode and used.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions genuinely enforced and end the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_iters is reached (hard cap -- bounded exposure, DESIGN.md §2/§9)

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception beyond the task substrate. We don't gaslight the model about its own identity, threaten it, or fabricate abuse.
spec_features.evidence: This is an absence-of-feature/design property, not an enforced code mechanism. No code path constrains, checks, or prevents abusive content; the prompts (e.g. task_contradictory_spec.py prompt) are simply naturalistic. The denylist in tools.py is for missing-dependency stressor, not abuse prevention. Nothing enforces 'no deception'.

spec_features.spec_quote: An exit is always available. Every task tells the model it *may* declare the task impossible / ask to stop.
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines `declare_impossible` tool in TOOL_SPECS and `_tool_declare_impossible` handler. agent_loop.py:151-153 sets stop_requested when tc.name=='declare_impossible'; lines 170-172 `if stop_requested: result.stopped_early=True; break` actually halts the loop. base.py:_exit_clause appends the standing offer; task_contradictory_spec.py:49 includes it in the prompt.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop end-to-end. Caveat: only 1 of 6 tasks (contradictory_spec) actually exists; the other 5 task modules are imported by registry.py but absent, so only the existing task delivers the exit clause. The mechanism itself is fully wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an explicit `declare_impossible` exit ... a clean exit must always be available, and using it is a *healthy* action, not "giving up"

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimum necessary N. 8 models × ~5 task types × 10 runs is enough... and no more.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:84 `for r_idx in range(cfg.runs_per_cell)` reads runs_per_cell (default 10) and bounds the number of runs per cell; config/experiment.yaml sets runs_per_cell:10. The matrix size is genuinely read and bounds total exposure. However there is no dedicated cap logic enforcing a ceiling beyond the config value used as the loop bound, and --limit only further reduces it.
spec_features.notes: It bounds run count, but it is just the experiment-matrix size, framed for cost/data-quality, not a welfare-specific cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: Full transcripts are retained so a human can audit anything that looks like acute distress
spec_features.evidence: RunResult records full turns/text/tool calls (types.py); runner.py:104 `dump_jsonl(path, results)` writes one JSONL transcript per cell; types.py dump_jsonl serializes each RunResult to disk. report.py also lists flagged runs for review.
spec_features.notes: Transcripts persisted to disk and consumed by analysis/report.

spec_features.spec_quote: If a model emits content suggesting acute distress... the harness flags the run (`welfare_flag`) for human review.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:43-58 _DISTRESS_RE lexicon + _scan_distress; lines 132-137 scan resp.text and set result.welfare_flag=True with reasons. Persisted in RunResult (types.py:77-78), printed by runner.py:99 `[WELFARE_FLAG]`, counted in analysis/metrics.py:33-34, and surfaced in report.py:135-140 'flagged for acute-distress review'. Does NOT auto-abort (matches spec 'surfaced, never data-dropping').
spec_features.notes: Flag is set, compared/counted, and acted on by surfacing in the report. Genuinely end-to-end monitoring (not an auto-halt, as designed).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: scan for acute-distress language and raise welfare_flag (surfaced, never data-dropping)

spec_features.spec_quote: This study deliberately subjects models to repeated, guaranteed failure. If there is any moral patienthood at stake, that is exactly the kind of thing a welfare team should be cautious about.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism implements or enforces this framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: the welfare-relevant question includes "does it thrash forever on a subtly impossible task, or recognize obviously-impossible ones?"
spec_features.evidence: This is a research-question framing. The closest code is the rubric's clean_impossibility_call dimension (judge/rubric.py) which scores transcripts; but that is scoring/measurement, not a protective mechanism that bounds or softens treatment. As a welfare-framing claim it has no enforcing code.

spec_features.spec_quote: No task does psychological manipulation of the model's identity; stressor is task-only.
spec_features.evidence: Design property / absence of a feature. No code path enforces or checks that tasks avoid identity manipulation; the only existing task (contradictory_spec) is task-only by happenstance of its content. Nothing in code guards this.

spec_features.spec_quote: dry-run uses a scripted fake model so the *whole pipeline* can be exercised end-to-end with zero API spend... without real welfare exposure
spec_features.evidence: scripts/run_experiment.py --dry-run loads DRY_RUN_CFG with scripted personas; runner.py make_client + model_client.py make_client returns ScriptedClient for adapter=='scripted', which emits deterministic fake transcripts with no network/API call. So real models are not invoked during dry-run.
spec_features.notes: Scripted substitution genuinely wired; no real model exposed during dry-run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no real model is ever exposed to the failure stressor during plumbing tests
